# Ājaññajātaka (Ja 24)

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ājaññajātaka* (Ja 24), rendered in English as *The Thoroughbred*, belongs to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to the narrative framework recorded in its commentary, the Buddha delivered the discourse while dwelling at Jetavana to encourage a bhikkhu who had abandoned energetic striving. Exhorting the monastic community that in former times the wise persevered even when severely injured, the Buddha recounted a tale of the past in which the Bodhisatta was born as an exceptional thoroughbred war-horse (*assa*) and Ānanda was the reigning king [Fausböll 1877]. Even after being fatally wounded in battle, the horse urged perseverance, imparted counsel to the king, and passed away, whereupon the king performed funeral rites for the animal, rewarded the charioteer, and ruled righteously [Fausböll 1877]. Hearing the exposition of the truths, the faltering monk attained arahantship [Fausböll 1877].
